surfaces.part: sand ground at foot of stairs

answer.evidence: The stairs repeat an 8-row cycle. Each cycle has 3-4 rows of light tread with block texture, then a 1-row bright front-edge line (rows 4, 12, 20, 28, 36, 44), then 3-4 rows of darker riser and shadow (for example x=24 goes L=170, 144, 118, 144 across rows 5-8). Every step therefore shows a top surface with an edge line above a front face, which matches the green cabinet and seat references and not the rim-only or front-elevation red ones. The darker strip on the left is a cliff-edge border, not a receding side face. The sand floor in rows 48-63 is flat ground.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a stair/cliff piece made of horizontal tan planks, with a flat sand strip across the bottom. Each material has only about 3 lightness steps (light, mid, dark brown edge). The dark edges are tinted brown, so 0% neutral and the outline reads as dark material tone. The sand strip is a large flat fill with only a few sparse dots, and the 23% near-flat coverage confirms flat areas where both references have 0%. Visible tones per tile (7) match the paving reference only because of the banded plank edges. They are well above the grass reference's 3, but the texture is mostly repeated stripes with no per-tile grain, speckle or individual shading. The 8 raw colours per tile and 10 in total are far below what the grass reference uses (26 per tile, 80 total). Next to the references it looks flatter and more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: stair treads (6 steps, repeating every 8 rows)
flat sand ground at the foot of the stairs

answer.evidence: Each step has a textured tread band (for example rows 1-3 and 9-11) that ends in a bright cream front-edge line (rows 4, 12, 20, 28, 36, 44). Below each line are 3-4 rows of darker riser and shadow (for example rows 5-8, 13-16, 21-24). The pattern repeats six times, so every step shows both a top surface and a south-facing front face. The sand at rows 48-63 is flat ground.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has tinted brown-tan edges (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so it avoids the black sticker outline. It reads as a few repeated horizontal step bands with light, mid and dark tan, about 4 steps. The sand apron at the bottom is mostly one flat tan with only sparse dots. Measured near-flat coverage is 23%, while both references are at 0%. Only 8 raw colours and 10 in total, against 26 and 80 for the grass. The 7 visible tones per tile match the paving, but the paving spreads them as per-stone shading across the whole tile. The candidate's tones sit in banded stripes with little grain or per-tile variation, so it looks flatter and simpler than the references. Not equal in craft, so fail when in doubt.

Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark brown beside the sand and wood, not a black sticker line. It has only 10 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference. Near-flat coverage is 23%, while both references are at 0%. By eye, the repeated step bands are a mechanical pattern of one light tan, one mid tan and a dark brown line, with little per-step variation or grain. Flat 5x5 areas and a limited palette make it look slightly flatter than the Beodeul bar, so I fail it when in doubt.
